headline: Anthropic founded by ex-OpenAI researchers led by the Amodeis
summary: Anthropic was founded at the beginning of 2021 (Delaware entity date January 26, 2021) by former OpenAI staff, with Dario Amodei as CEO and Daniela Amodei as President, alongside co-founders Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Tom Brown, Chris Olah, Sam McCandlish and Ben Mann.
governance: Founded as a public benefit corporation; mission framed as AI safety and research ('steerable, interpretable, robust' systems).
moat: Founding team wrote the GPT-3 and scaling-laws work at OpenAI (per Core Views page).
strategy: Initially research-first; commercialization 'down the road' (TechCrunch, May 2021).
people: Dario Amodei (Co-founder & CEO (ex-OpenAI VP of Research), joined); Daniela Amodei (Co-founder & President (ex-OpenAI VP Safety & Policy), joined); Jack Clark (Co-founder, Head of Policy, joined); Jared Kaplan (Co-founder, joined); Tom Brown (Co-founder, joined); Chris Olah (Co-founder, joined); Sam McCandlish (Co-founder, joined); Ben Mann (Co-founder, joined)

Founder list is from T4 sources (Wikipedia citing CNBC 2025 and Reuters 2023, which I could not open); Anthropic sometimes describes seven co-founders. Contrary Research says 'December 2020' and that 15 researchers left OpenAI — see conflicts.

headline: Incorporated as Delaware public benefit corporation with stated public benefit
summary: Anthropic incorporated in Delaware as a Public Benefit Corporation whose 2021 charter states the specific public benefit as 'to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the cultural, social and technological improvement of humanity' (later reworded to 'long term benefit of humanity').
governance: Delaware PBC: directors may balance stockholder financial interests against the charter's public benefit purpose (Anthropic LTBT post). Earliest (2021) charter purpose: 'responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the cultural, social and technological improvement of humanity'; later versions: 'for the long term benefit of humanity'.
notes: PBC status is T1-confirmed (Anthropic LTBT post, Series A page footer, company page). The exact 2021 charter wording is quoted by a T4 blog from Delaware filings I could not open; date of the original certificate assumed equal to the entity date (Jan 26, 2021).

headline: Series A documents create 'Long-Term Benefit Committee', LTBT precursor
summary: An earlier version of the Long-Term Benefit Trust, called the Long-Term Benefit Committee, was written into Anthropic's 2021 Series A documents, the origin of the governance mechanism later formalized (with Class T stock) at the Series C.
governance: LTBT lineage: 'Long-Term Benefit Committee' in 2021 Series A docs -> Long-Term Benefit Trust formalized at Series C via amended charter creating Class T stock that elects/removes directors on time- and funding-based milestones (majority of board within 4 years).
notes: Anthropic states the committee was in the 2021 Series A documents; exact execution date not given, so dated to the Series A announcement month. Formal LTBT announcement (Sept 19, 2023) is out of this scout's period.

headline: First alignment paper: 'General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment'
summary: Anthropic's first major alignment paper (Askell et al., 22 authors, arXiv 2112.00861) framed the 'helpful, honest, harmless' assistant as a testbed and found ranked preference modeling scales better than imitation learning.
moat: Establishes the HHH (helpful/honest/harmless) framing that underpins Claude's later training.
people: Amanda Askell (First author, None)

headline: Publishes 'A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits'
summary: Anthropic's interpretability team (Elhage, Nanda, Olsson et al., 25 authors) published the foundational mechanistic-interpretability framework for reverse-engineering attention-only transformers and identified 'induction heads'.
moat: Mechanistic interpretability program led by co-founder Chris Olah; author list (25 names incl. all founders) is a proxy for the research staff at end-2021.
people: Nelson Elhage (First author, None); Chris Olah (Corresponding author / interpretability lead, None); Neel Nanda (Co-author (Anthropic, 2021), None)

headline: 'Predictability and Surprise' policy paper, later presented at FAccT '22
summary: Ganguli et al. (30 authors, arXiv 2202.07785) argued that large generative models combine predictable scaling-law loss with unpredictable specific capabilities, framing Anthropic's policy case for pre-deployment evaluation; accepted to ACM FAccT '22.
strategy: Positions Anthropic as a policy voice on emergent-capability risk; ties to Jack Clark's 2022 government engagements.
people: Deep Ganguli (First author, None)

headline: 'In-context Learning and Induction Heads' interpretability result
summary: Anthropic published research arguing that induction heads are the circuit mechanism behind in-context learning in transformers, extending the December 2021 framework.
notes: Author list not shown on the anthropic.com summary page.

headline: First version of Claude trained in spring 2022, withheld from release
summary: Anthropic trained the first version of its headline model, Claude, in spring 2022 and chose to prioritize it for internal safety research rather than public deployment, citing race-dynamics concerns.
strategy: Deliberate non-release of a frontier-class model in 2022 to avoid accelerating a race; public release came March 2023 (scout-2023).
notes: Date precision is seasonal ('spring 2022' per Anthropic); Wikipedia says training finished 'summer 2022' — recorded in conflicts. Date field is a placeholder for Q2 2022. Model-size claims not verified.

headline: RLHF 'helpful and harmless assistant' paper released
summary: Bai et al. (31 authors, arXiv 2204.05862) applied preference modeling and reinforcement learning from human feedback to train a helpful and harmless assistant, finding alignment training improved almost all NLP evaluations — the technical basis of Claude's training.
moat: Core RLHF recipe (with the accompanying HH-RLHF dataset) used for Claude.
people: Yuntao Bai (First author, None)

headline: Model lifecycle: Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5 retirement windows open
summary: Anthropic's deprecations page (2026-09-30) shows Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.6 active with retirement 'not sooner than' dates into 2027, while Sonnet 4.5 (Sep 29, 2026), Haiku 4.5 (Oct 15, 2026) and Opus 4.5 (Nov 24, 2026) become eligible for retirement first.
notes: Policy: at least 60 days' notice before retirement of publicly released models; Anthropic commits to preserving model weights (deprecation-commitments page referenced, not opened). Typical model life before retirement: Claude 1/Instant ~20 months; Claude 3 Opus ~22 months; Sonnet 4/Opus 4 ~13 months.

headline: No public Anthropic S-1 on EDGAR; SpaceX and Nscale filings cite it
summary: As of Sept 30 an EDGAR company search for 'anthropic' returns no matching companies and full-text search for 'Anthropic PBC' in S-1 forms surfaces only SpaceX, Nscale, Figma and Idea Acquisition filings, consistent with a June 1 confidential draft and a prospectus seen only through leaks.
notes: Absence-of-record finding (T1 search results): consistent with a confidential draft submission. Other issuers' draft filings appear on EDGAR only after the public S-1 (e.g., SpaceX DRS of 2026-03-30 and DRS/A of 2026-05-07 are now listed alongside its S-1). Forkast (Sep 25) independently says 'As of September 26, the SEC EDGAR database contains no public Anthropic filing'. Re-check before relying on it; every prospectus figure in this file is therefore leak-based (T2/T3), never T1.

headline: PitchBook ledger totals $126.754B; $34.5B chip bonds no longer included
summary: PitchBook's Sep 30 deal list sums to $126,754M (Series H 'Raised to Date') with no chip-financing record, versus $161,254M reported on Jul 16 when the $34.5B bonds (PB deal 334763-02T) were counted.
notes: FLAG. Arithmetic: 161,254 - 126,754 = 34,500 exactly. The Sep-30 extract contains no record for deal 334763-02T, so PB removed or reclassified it; the reason is not stated anywhere I could open (pitchbook.com profile/news pages return 403; search snippet shows PitchBook saying Anthropic 'has raised $127 billion'). Press explains why it should not count: the notes are issued by a lessor SPV and Anthropic only leases (5-year lease; Broadcom backstop), although a 'chip bonds' label makes it look like Anthropic debt. The $161.254B figure is therefore an over-count; use $126.754B (incl. $2.5B revolver) or $124.254B (equity only).
